document_summary: Massachusetts General Laws c. 186, § 12, setting notice periods to terminate a tenancy at will (three months' notice, or 14 days for nonpayment of rent), with a right to cure within ten days.

rules.title: M.G.L. c. 186 § 12 - Notice to determine estate at will
rules.requirement: A tenancy at will may be ended by either party with three months' written notice (or the rent interval/30 days if longer), or by 14 days' notice to quit for nonpayment of rent, subject to a one-time-per-12-months right to cure within ten days.
rules.key_value: 3 months' written notice; 14 days' notice for nonpayment
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party;
rules.out_of_scope_reason: General notice-to-quit period, not a limit on grounds for eviction; excluded from just-cause scope.
rules.extraction_notes: No effective date stated in the source text. Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause eviction statute; this section is only a notice-to-quit provision.
